newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - June 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - June 5.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Sears, Roebuck and Co has agreed to pay about $100 million to 200,000 consumers as part of a settlement for its "flawed" credit-card collection practices.
* A plan to move Big Board stocks from fractions to decimals is expected to come up for a vote.
* PepsiCo Inc stock dropped amid concerns about cut-throat pricing and persistent rumours that it plans to spin off its bottling business.
* Eli Lilly and Co may end up writing off a large portion of the $4.1 billion it paid to buy PCS Health Systems Inc.
* Ford Motor Co's U.S. sales of light-vehicles dropped 3 percent in May.

* Donna Karan International Inc is searching for an outside executive to take over the day-to-day operations of the fashion house so its founder, Donna Karan, can focus more on the creative end of things.
* The top four U.S. television networks generated about $6 billion in advance sales of TV ad time for the next season, an increase of about 6 percent over the prior year.
* H.F. Ahmanson and Co dropped its bid to acquire Great Western Financial Corp, getting out of the way of rival suitor, Washington Mutual Inc.
* Brazil sold $3 billion in 30-year bonds in what is believed to be the second-largest global bond offering.
* Chrysler Corp is expected to announce that cost-saving measures presented by their suppliers will increase its 1997 profit by $325 million.
* The Internal Revenue Service was ordered to pay a Colorado woman $325,000 for disclosing details of her tax returns to the media.
* McDonald's Corp's decision to abandon the bulk of its 55-cent sandwich promotion led some analysts to cut their estimates -- and question the future of senior management.
* The USDA is investigating alleged anticompetitive practices in the meatpacking industry, and possible unfair dealings with poultry producers.
* A federal judge in Pennsylvania has denied class-action status to a lawsuit brought on behalf of smokers in that state.
* The Dow Jones industrials dropped 42.49 points, resting at 7269.66.

* Heard on the Street: Are Kmart's troubles really behind it? In recent months, Wall Street has become enthusiastic about Kmart's turnaround story, sending its shares soaring from 10 to a high of nearly 15. But now, a few doubts are creeping in.
* Credit Markets: Brazil became the latest issuer to surf the wave of cash flowing into emerging-market bonds with yesterday's massive $3 billion offering of 30-year dollar-denominated global funds.
